key_insight: Poorer baseline prognosis was associated with greater survival benefit from chemotherapy-containing regimens versus pembrolizumab alone in head and neck and urothelial cancers, with a less certain pattern in lung cancer.
clinical_relevance: These findings question the assumption that immunotherapy alone necessarily offers better outcomes for patients with poorer prognosis.
method: Emulated five first-line treatment trials using US electronic health records across advanced solid tumors.
Used machine learning to predict baseline 6-month survival.
Applied overlap-weighted regression to assess treatment differences in 2-year restricted mean survival time by prognosis.
evidence_signal: Among 8,688 patients treated during 2011–2023, prognosis-related treatment differences were significant in head and neck and urothelial cancers, while immunotherapy improved overall restricted mean survival in colorectal cancer and melanoma without clear variation by prognosis.
watch_item: This observational treatment-comparison study—not AI drug discovery—may retain residual confounding and does not establish individualized treatment recommendations.
paper_title: Baseline Prognosis and Treatment Benefit From First-Line Immunotherapy Strategies: Target Trial Emulations Across Advanced Solid Tumors
